gumtree_entries.description: ADDED i3: The chronology under test: an accounting calendar whose years end on the SUNDAY nearest the end of AUGUST, are split into thirteen even 4-week months, and place
ADDED i6: Pairs of equivalent dates: an {@link AccountingDate} and the ISO {@link LocalDate} it maps to. Used to verify conversions in both directions.
ADDED i7: Year/month/day combinations that are out of range and must be rejected by {@link AccountingChronology#date(int, int, int)}.
ADDED i15: A year is an accounting leap year when it spans 371 days (53 weeks) instead of the usual 364 (52 weeks).
ADDED i16: Each row is {year, month, expected length-of-month}. Regular months are 28 days; month 13 carries the leap-week so it is 35 days in a leap year.
ADDED i20: Each row is {year, month, day, field, expectedMin, expectedMax} describing the valid range of {@code field} for the given date.
ADDED i22: Each row is {year, month, day, field, expectedValue} for {@code getLong(field)}.
ADDED i24: Each row is {year, month, day, field, newValue, expectedYear, expectedMonth, expectedDay}: setting {@code field} to {@code newValue} on the start date yields th
ADDED i29: Each row is {year, month, day, amount, unit, expectedYear, expectedMonth, expectedDay}: adding {@code amount} of {@code unit} to the start date yields the expec
ADDED i30: Reuses data_plus rows in reverse: subtracting amount from the "plus result" (year/month/dom) must return the original start date (expected*).
ADDED i32: Each row is {year1, month1, day1, year2, month2, day2, unit, expectedAmount}: the distance from the first date to the second, measured in {@code unit}.
ADDED i35: A chronology with different settings (ends on WEDNESDAY, year anchored to the ISO year it ends in) so its dates form their own equality group.
ADDED i37: Each row is {date, expected toString()}. The {@code other} chronology differs from {@link #INSTANCE} only in that its year starts (rather than ends) in the give
